decisions.statement: Retained legacy migration backups must be ignored by Git
decisions.reasoning: Backups may contain generated state, telemetry, credentials, or historical files and exist only for local recovery.
consequences: Migration ensures the backup pattern is present in the project .gitignore before publication.

decisions.statement: Self-hosted quality gates must reference tools installed by the repository
decisions.reasoning: A migrated command can be syntactically safe yet unavailable in the current project, causing false operational failure.
consequences: The AutoForge repository retains typecheck, formatting, and test gates but removes its unavailable ESLint gate.

decisions.statement: Quality command timeouts must terminate the entire spawned process tree
decisions.reasoning: Killing only an npm parent leaves test runners active, causes resource contention, and makes later checks nondeterministic.
consequences: Use an isolated POSIX process group and group termination, with direct child termination as the portable fallback.

decisions.statement: Foundation tests must use bounded worker concurrency
decisions.reasoning: Running every test file at default parallelism creates filesystem and process contention that causes otherwise passing integration tests to exceed local timeouts.
consequences: Vitest uses at most four workers while preserving per-file isolation and existing timeouts.

decisions.statement: Intent is a durable typed artifact linked to work, specifications, and research.
decisions.reasoning: Intent must preserve raw user input and progressively structured fields without pretending incomplete information is complete.
consequences: Add an intent schema and registry-backed storage; work items reference intent IDs.

decisions.statement: Triage is a deterministic multi-label service.
decisions.reasoning: The same request must produce repeatable classifications before any agent-specific behavior or model call.
consequences: Implement pure triage rules with explicit evidence and golden fixtures.

decisions.statement: Readiness is an explainable heuristic, never a claim of certainty.
decisions.reasoning: Missing requirements must remain visible and confidence scores must not hide unknowns.
consequences: Return known fields, missing evidence, labels, and an optional bounded score.

decisions.statement: Research records are first-class linked artifacts.
decisions.reasoning: Research findings, sources, alternatives, and recommendations need durable provenance and must connect to decisions and specifications.
consequences: Add a research specification type with confidence and source metadata.

decisions.statement: Planning artifacts are modular projections, not a monolithic generated document.
decisions.reasoning: Different requests require different planning outputs and irrelevant context should remain excluded.
consequences: Compile feature briefs, technical plans, design briefs, stories, and acceptance criteria independently.

decisions.statement: 0.8 extends the v0.7 registry and packet contracts additively.
decisions.reasoning: Existing work, state, specification, resolver, adapter, and packet behavior is the released compatibility baseline.
consequences: Preserve current IDs and formats; add migrations only for unavoidable schema changes.

decisions.statement: The 0.8 architecture decision set is approved as the baseline for schema implementation.
decisions.reasoning: The reviewed decisions preserve v0.7 compatibility while defining intent, triage, readiness, research, and modular planning boundaries.
consequences: Proceed to resolve the remaining schema-level decisions, then implement intent and research contracts.

decisions.statement: Intent is stored as a registry-backed specification with raw and structured fields; work stores only the intent reference.
decisions.reasoning: Intent is project knowledge and should use the existing specification identity, relationships, codec, and resolver rather than a parallel state domain.
consequences: Add an intent type and preserve raw input plus optional structured fields in the specification body and metadata.

decisions.statement: One intent may produce multiple work items through explicit intent relationships.
decisions.reasoning: A single request can yield research, design, architecture, and implementation tasks without duplicating the source intent.
consequences: Use typed outgoing work references and preserve independent lifecycle state for each work item.

decisions.statement: Triage labels are additive; conflicts are reported rather than hidden by precedence.
decisions.reasoning: Requests can legitimately require research and design or clarification and architecture at the same time.
consequences: Return all matching labels, evidence, and a conflict flag; do not collapse the result to one winner.

decisions.statement: Readiness requires objective evidence fields and reports missing evidence by work kind.
decisions.reasoning: A universal checklist would overstate readiness for different request classes.
consequences: Define minimum evidence profiles for implementation, research, architecture, and design work.

decisions.statement: Readiness confidence uses a bounded categorical level plus an optional percentage for display.
decisions.reasoning: Categories communicate uncertainty better while a bounded percentage supports progress reporting.
consequences: Every score includes evidence and missing-field explanations; no score is treated as a guarantee.

decisions.statement: Research sources require provenance type, locator, captured timestamp, and confidence when available.
decisions.reasoning: Research must remain auditable across local files, URLs, agent observations, and human notes.
consequences: Represent sources as typed records and permit unavailable locators only with an explicit explanation.

decisions.statement: The canonical v0.8 token type remains token; design-token is a documentation alias only.
decisions.reasoning: The v0.7 registry already ships token IDs and changing the prefix would create unnecessary migration risk.
consequences: Accept token in schemas and map any imported design-token terminology to token without changing identity.

decisions.statement: Generated planning artifacts store source fingerprints and freshness metadata.
decisions.reasoning: Planning outputs must be reproducible and visibly stale when their inputs change.
consequences: Persist generated artifacts with source IDs, revisions or hashes, generator version, and generated timestamp.

decisions.statement: Antigravity and agy are aliases for the canonical gemini agent contract
decisions.reasoning: The Gemini adapter already delivers both Gemini CLI and Antigravity instructions, while maintaining separate capability IDs would create drift. Aliases preserve user-facing terminology without duplicating contracts.
consequences: Normalize antigravity and agy to gemini when generating contracts; keep gemini as the canonical agentId and capability definition.

decisions.statement: Every implementation change must update the relevant documentation before completion
decisions.reasoning: AutoForge is used by multiple agentic AIs and users; undocumented behavior creates drift between the CLI, contracts, workflows, and actual implementation.
consequences: Each task must identify affected documentation, update it within scope, and include documentation validation in its completion evidence.

decisions.statement: Project-scoped single-file stores must resolve null instead of throwing ENOENT before initialization
decisions.reasoning: Constitution, domain, and planning stores crashed with raw uncaught ENOENT stack traces when read before init, unlike the twin store's graceful null-return convention discovered during a north-star roadmap coverage audit. Every command using these stores must handle a null result.
consequences: ConstitutionStore.load(), DomainStore.load(), and PlanningArtifactStore.read()/isFresh() now return null/false on a missing file; new callers must null-check before use.
CLI commands report a friendly EXIT_CODE.invalidState message naming the init command instead of an unhandled exception.

decisions.statement: Issue and task completion requires a linked decision record or an explicit, audited skip reason
decisions.reasoning: CHANGELOG.md silently stopped tracking releases after v0.6.0 because documentation was advisory rather than enforced, and this was only discovered by manual audit across agent handoffs where no human was present to catch the omission.
consequences: autoforge done blocks issue/task completion without a relatedWork-linked decision; autoforge done --no-decision <reason> bypasses it but records the reason as a skip-reason decision.
autoforge changelog compile renders bugfix/feature-note decisions since the last tag into CHANGELOG.md, closing the specific gap that motivated this change.

decisions.statement: Both P0 issues (empty-rationale crash, deferred/conflict false positives) were already fixed in 0.21.x before being filed against a stale 0.20.3 install
decisions.reasoning: Independently verified by pulling the published v0.20.3 tarball: recommendWorkflow in workflow.ts pushed to stages for RESEARCH_REQUIRED/ARCHITECTURE_REQUIRED/DESIGN_REQUIRED/PLANNING_REQUIRED with no matching rationale.push(), and triage.ts had no textSegments() sentence-boundary function, using bare word regexes and an unbounded conflict pattern against a flat-joined blob -- both exactly matching the filed bug reports. Both are fixed in current source (confirmed by direct execution against the described repro cases) and in the published v0.21.0 tarball. The reporting session was running a stale global pnpm install (v0.20.3) due to pnpm's minimumReleaseAgeExclude gate silently no-opping a plain 'pnpm add -g ...@latest'.
consequences: Closed issue.fix-recommend-workflow-empty-rationale-crash and issue.fix-intent-triage-deferred-conflict-keyword-false-positives as already-fixed-in-0.21.x, not live defects.
Global pnpm autoforge install on this machine updated to 0.21.1 via --force; npm dist-tags confirmed latest correctly points to 0.21.1.

Worth a future advisory: recommend 'npx @cojacklabs/autoforge@latest' or 'autoforge update' over 'pnpm add -g ...@latest' for global installs, since pnpm's release-age gate can silently hold back updates without warning.

decisions.statement: recommendWorkflow's empty-rationale crash was already fixed before this issue was filed
decisions.reasoning: The reporting session ran a stale global pnpm install (v0.20.3), where RESEARCH_REQUIRED/ARCHITECTURE_REQUIRED/DESIGN_REQUIRED/PLANNING_REQUIRED pushed to stages with no matching rationale.push(). Verified fixed in current source and in the published v0.21.0 tarball by direct execution of the exact repro case.
consequences: No code change required; global pnpm install corrected to 0.21.1.

decisions.statement: Intent triage deferred/conflict regex false positives were already fixed before this issue was filed
decisions.reasoning: The reporting session ran a stale global pnpm install (v0.20.3), where textSegments() did not exist and deferred/conflict regexes matched an unbounded, unsegmented joined blob of all intent fields. Verified fixed in current source and in the published v0.21.0 tarball: textSegments() splits on sentence boundaries before matching, and both regexes are word/sentence-bounded. Tested the exact false-positive examples from the issue report directly; both correctly return false against current source.
consequences: No code change required; global pnpm install corrected to 0.21.1.

decisions.statement: bootstrap approve verb was already implemented before this issue was filed
decisions.reasoning: approveBootstrapArtifact() and 'autoforge bootstrap approve <artifact-id> [--evidence <path|workflow-id>]' fully exist, writing status:approved plus approvedAt and validated evidence into manifest.json. Confirmed absent in the reporting session's stale v0.20.3 install.
consequences: No code change required.

decisions.statement: Intent and workflow kind vocabularies were already unified before this issue was filed
decisions.reasoning: src/core/vocabularies.ts is a shared single source-of-truth module: READINESS_WORK_KINDS, WORKFLOW_KINDS, INTENT_TO_WORKFLOW_KINDS mapping, normalizeWorkflowKind() aliasing, and workflowKindHelp() for actionable error text. Confirmed absent in the reporting session's stale v0.20.3 install.
consequences: No code change required for this specific ask; data/security kinds remain a separate, still-live gap tracked as its own issue.

decisions.statement: workflow command already surfaces real errors instead of a bare catch before this issue was filed
decisions.reasoning: runWorkflowCommand's catch block calls reportCommandError, which distinguishes ZodError, AutoForgeError, ENOENT, and generic errors with real messages, and invalid workflow kinds get an explicit message plus workflowKindHelp() text. Confirmed the bare catch {} described in the issue is absent in current source and was absent even in the reporting session's stale v0.20.3 install path for this specific function.
consequences: No code change required for the described defect. Noted separately: a stray orphaned import statement after the function body in src/commands/workflow.ts is a minor cleanup candidate, unrelated to this issue's described defect.

decisions.statement: Introspectable JSON schemas for file-accepting commands already existed before this issue was filed
decisions.reasoning: The --schema flag exists on intent assess, research register, workflow handoff, bootstrap discover, and others; a dedicated autoforge schemas list and schemas show command covers nine schemas total. Confirmed absent in the reporting sessions stale v0.20.3 install.
consequences: No code change required.

decisions.statement: The bootstrap to intent/workflow/design/planning relationship was already documented before this issue was filed
decisions.reasoning: docs/BOOTSTRAP_PIPELINE.md exists, is linked from README, and walks through exactly the relationship requested: bootstrap tracks artifact status only, intent/workflow/design/planning are the production mechanisms, and approvals connect completed work back to the manifest. Confirmed absent in the reporting sessions stale v0.20.3 install.
consequences: No code change required.

decisions.statement: Added dedicated data and security work kinds to the shared intent/workflow vocabulary
decisions.reasoning: Bootstrap's gate list requires data and security artifacts but no correctly-labeled intent or workflow kind existed for either; users had to mislabel this work as architecture.
consequences: READINESS_WORK_KINDS and WORKFLOW_KINDS gained data/data-change and security/security-change; both have dedicated workflow definitions with research(optional)->planning->implementation->validation(required) stages.

decisions.statement: Persisted planning artifacts are now namespaced by source fingerprint instead of a flat kind-only path
decisions.reasoning: intent assess --artifact <kind> --persist previously wrote to a fixed .autoforge/planning/<kind>.json path, silently overwriting any prior artifact of the same kind with no warning.
consequences: PlanningArtifactStore stores artifacts at .autoforge/planning/<kind>/<sourceFingerprint>.json; read(kind) with no fingerprint returns the most recent version; a new listVersions(kind) method and updated planning list surface every stored version.

decisions.statement: Newly registered projects now default to an active lifecycle, and the mutation-blocked error names the exact fix command
decisions.reasoning: registerProject left lifecycle undefined, which projectMutationBlocked treats as blocked while projects list/show already displayed it as active -- an undiscoverable, inconsistent trap that silently blocked every mutating use command against a freshly attached project.
consequences: registerProject sets lifecycle: active on first registration (preserving an existing explicit lifecycle on re-registration); the blocked-command stderr message now includes the exact autoforge projects update --lifecycle active fix.

decisions.statement: Generated user-stories artifacts no longer mangle acronyms or repeat the objective clause on every line
decisions.reasoning: The prior template called toLowerCase() on the full requirement string, destroying leading acronyms/proper nouns, and appended a generic so the stated objective is achieved phrase verbatim to every single requirement line, producing barely grammatical boilerplate.
consequences: The user-stories template now lowercases only a non-acronym leading word, strips redundant trailing punctuation before appending a period, and states the shared objective once in a header line instead of once per story. Actor extraction and compound-requirement splitting remain explicitly out of scope as a separate, harder NLP problem.

decisions.statement: The documentation gate genuinely improved release hygiene across v0.21.1 and v0.21.2
decisions.reasoning: Both releases shipped with accurate CHANGELOG.md entries auto-compiled from linked decisions, closing the exact gap that motivated the documentation-gate feature.
consequences: Confirms the hypothesis; no further changes needed to the documentation gate itself.

decisions.statement: Extended the README/AGENT_SETUP_GUIDE canonical startup prompt to point agents at AUTOFORGE_CLI_REFERENCE.md, brought that reference doc current with the learning and changelog command families, and removed hardcoded version numbers from documentation prose
decisions.reasoning: Solo devs need a single copy/paste onboarding artifact that both bootstraps an agent into AutoForge's governed workflow and points it at a genuinely current command catalog, so the agent can govern/scaffold/categorize/prioritize work using the full CLI rather than guessing. The reference doc had drifted since v0.21 and was missing the entire learning/evidence surface and changelog compile shipped in v0.22.0.
consequences: Future doc edits in this repo must never introduce a version number into prose; AUTOFORGE_CLI_REFERENCE.md needs a manual side-by-side check against src/cli/help.ts on future command additions since there is no automated drift check (deliberately out of scope)

decisions.statement: autoforge why surfaces linked evidence beneath each matched decision
decisions.reasoning: The v0.22 Learning & Evidence Engine design spec required an Evidence: line in why's decision output whenever evidence records reference a decision via resultingDecision, but no v0.22 implementation task covered src/decisions/search.ts or src/commands/why.ts, so the data was correctly linked but never surfaced to the primary human/agent-facing query command.
consequences: runWhyCommand now loads the EvidenceStore, groups records by resultingDecision, and formatDecisionMatches appends an Evidence: <id>, <id> line to each matched decision block when applicable; two new why.test.ts cases cover the line's presence and its absence.

decisions.statement: projects list --json already existed before this issue was filed; the duplicated list-handling branches were consolidated into one
decisions.reasoning: Investigation showed runProjectsCommand had two separate code paths both handling action === list: an early branch entered only when --json appeared in the projectPath or flag slot, and a later branch handling every other list invocation including the bare default. Both built the same JSON/table output independently, which is confusing to maintain and made a bare autoforge projects command depend on defaulting logic duplicated in two places.
consequences: runProjectsCommand now defaults a missing action to list once, and a single list branch at the bottom of the function handles bare list, list --json, and list <name> --json uniformly; the redundant early-return branch was removed. Added test coverage for the no-args default-to-list path and for rejecting a non---json trailing flag on list.

decisions.statement: The ultimate north-star guide is now version-number-consistent with the authoritative revised roadmap
decisions.reasoning: docs/planning/NORTH_STAR_CONSISTENCY_AUDIT.md flagged that dev/AUTOFORGE_ULTIMATE_NORTH_STAR_v0.8-v0.25.md retained a phantom v0.15.0 Interactive AutoForge CLI milestone and off-by-one numbering for v0.16-v0.20 (Governance through Digital Twin) predating the roadmap revision that moved the Interactive CLI Experience to v0.25. This made the two north-star documents disagree on what version number corresponds to which engine from v0.15 through v0.20.
consequences: Renumbered v0.16-v0.20 down by one (Governance=v0.15, Domain Intelligence=v0.16, Design Protocol=v0.17, Traceability=v0.18, Validation=v0.19, Digital Twin stays v0.20), replaced the phantom v0.15.0 Interactive CLI section with a superseded-milestone notice pointing to the revised doc's v0.25 section, fixed the dependency-chain diagram and Phase 1/Phase 2 seam description, and corrected the Core Engine Model's Foundation vs Product Intelligence engine lists. Both north-star documents are now numbering-consistent from v0.8 through v0.25; the revised doc remains authoritative for narrative sequencing rationale.

decisions.statement: The strategy assessment schema, atomic-file store, and service are implemented and tested
decisions.reasoning: v0.23 (Product Strategy & Prioritization Engine) needed a durable, append-only record type for explainable multi-factor strategy judgments, persisted via the same lazy-init AtomicStateStore pattern as evidence/hypothesis/experiment, with a service layer that unconditionally links every assessment to a decision record.
consequences: src/strategy/strategy-schemas.ts, strategy-store.ts, and strategy-service.ts exist with full test coverage (schema validation, store idempotency, service validation/supersede/linked-decision behavior); StrategyService.history() tiebreaks by array position on equal createdAt timestamps, a fix caught during implementation review and applied beyond the original plan text.

decisions.statement: autoforge strategy assess/list/show/history is implemented and registered in the CLI
decisions.reasoning: v0.23 needed a human-facing command surface to record and query strategy assessments, mirroring the argument-parsing and error conventions already established by autoforge decide and autoforge learning evidence.
consequences: src/commands/strategy.ts implements all four actions; src/cli/index.ts, src/cli/help.ts, and src/cli/router.ts (the last not called out explicitly in the original plan, but required for the build to typecheck) register the command; 15 command-level tests cover valid assessment, invalid factor rejection, all 10 required-flag omissions, list filtering, show, and supersede/history ordering.

decisions.statement: The active work item's active strategy assessment is surfaced in context packets as an optional, non-budgeted field
decisions.reasoning: An agent picking up work should see why it was (or wasn't) prioritized, matching the principle that relevant decisions are already surfaced in context. Strategy assessments are a deterministic single-lookup per work item, not a ranked candidate pool, so they were modeled after the existing optional workflow/contract fields rather than routed through the budgeted doctrines/decisions/specs candidate system.
consequences: ContextSelection gained an optional strategy field (src/context/schemas.ts) excluded from the budget-consistency superRefine and uniqueness checks; renderStrategy (src/context/packet.ts) renders it unconditionally when present, including an assessment ID line added during implementation to satisfy the design's own worked example; compileProjectContext (src/commands/context.ts) looks up the active work item's active assessment directly, without modifying src/context/resolver.ts.

decisions.statement: The strategy command family is documented in the CLI reference
decisions.reasoning: docs/AUTOFORGE_CLI_REFERENCE.md is the canonical, currently-maintained command surface reference agents and users are pointed to at onboarding; undocumented commands create drift between the CLI and the reference.
consequences: A new Strategy and Prioritization section was added directly after Memory and Planning, documenting all four strategy commands and the deliberate distinction from orchestrate prioritize. CHANGELOG.md was intentionally left untouched since its entries are compiler-generated from linked decisions at release time.

decisions.statement: Global npm/yarn/pnpm install is now the advertised primary onboarding path
decisions.reasoning: README's Install section taught npm install --save-dev + npx as the first and only method, directly contradicting the README's own Starting From Scratch section which already assumed a globally installed CLI, and contradicting update.ts's existing global-vs-local install detection which already supports this. AutoForge is a long-lived per-machine control plane (global workspace registry, global agent contracts, cross-project history) that fits a global install; local --save-dev is the correct fallback only for environments that cannot retain a persistent global install.
consequences: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and docs/QUICKSTART.md now lead with npm/yarn/pnpm --global install and bare autoforge commands, with local --save-dev + npx demoted to an explicitly-scoped fallback section. docs/QUICKSTART.md, which described an entirely different and no-longer-existing AutoForge product (autopilot levels, recipes, a training loop, and commands like autopilot/train/metrics/dryrun/upgrade/snapshot/status/load that are absent from autoforge help), was rewritten from scratch against the actual current command surface and linked from README so it is no longer orphaned. CONTRIBUTING.md's references to the also-nonexistent configure/validate/load/snapshot commands were replaced with the real gate check/typecheck/test equivalents.

decisions.statement: Onboarding prompts now default to autoforge attach, not init, for new projects
decisions.reasoning: autoforge init only creates local .autoforge/ state; it never calls GlobalWorkspaceStore.registerProject(). autoforge attach <path> is the command that does both in one step, confirmed by reading src/commands/attach.ts and init.ts directly. Every onboarding surface (README's canonical prompt, the agent setup guide, and QUICKSTART.md) told agents to run init as the default path, phrased attach as an optional alternative, and never explained the consequence -- so agents following the docs exactly produced projects invisible to autoforge projects list, exactly as the user reported observing.
consequences: README.md, docs/AUTOFORGE_AGENT_SETUP_GUIDE.md, and docs/QUICKSTART.md now default new-project setup to autoforge attach "$PWD", explain that plain init does not register the project globally, and reserve init for a deliberately local-only install (e.g. a disposable CI container).

decisions.statement: The twin node-type schema was extended and renamed for v0.24
decisions.reasoning: The digital twin's node-type enum already anticipated constitution and domain but never gained dedicated types for phases/tasks/issues, strategy assessments, validation evidence, or traceability links, and reused the generic flow/work/risk labels as placeholders for work items -- colliding with specifications' own flow type once design specs would be projected.
consequences: twinNodeTypeSchema now includes phase, task, issue, strategy, validation-evidence, and trace-link; risk and work were removed since they had no other use in the codebase.

decisions.statement: Work phases, tasks, and issues now project into the digital twin with their own dedicated node types
decisions.reasoning: The twin previously reused the generic flow/work/risk node-type labels for phases/tasks/issues, which would have collided with specifications' own flow type once design specs were projected into the twin in a later task of this same milestone.
consequences: projectStateToTwin now emits type: phase/task/issue for WorkState phases/tasks/issues; flow and risk are now free to mean exactly what the rest of the codebase already calls them.

decisions.statement: Constitution rules and domain concepts now project into the digital twin
decisions.reasoning: The north-star's digital twin was always meant to include governance and domain, but the twin projection never populated nodes of those already-declared types. Closing this gap required reusing selectApplicableRules for governance-edge matching rather than evaluateGovernance, since the latter needs an objective string and computes pass/warning/conflict/blocked status that is unnecessary for a structural governs edge.
consequences: projectStateToTwin projects constitution rules as constitution nodes with governs edges to matching work items, and domain concepts as domain nodes with edges from domain.relationships and models edges to decision/specification provenance.

decisions.statement: Design specifications, active strategy assessments, traceability links, and validation evidence now project into the digital twin
decisions.reasoning: Closing the north-star's full-loop mandate for the twin required the remaining four data sources: specifications project using their own type field directly (safe only because the prior task freed flow from meaning a work phase), strategy assessments are filtered to active status only so superseded assessments never appear as stale current-state nodes, and traceability/validation-evidence edges rely entirely on buildTwinProjection's existing filter for edges referencing unmodeled nodes rather than reimplementing that check.
consequences: projectStateToTwin now projects specifications by their own type, active strategy assessments with assesses/resulted-in edges, traceability links as traces edges, and validation evidence as validation-evidence nodes with validates/traces edges.

decisions.statement: autoforge twin generate now reads all six new domains and includes them in the generated projection
decisions.reasoning: projectStateToTwin gained the ability to project governance, domain, specifications, strategy, traceability, and validation evidence, but nothing in the CLI actually read those stores yet.
consequences: runTwinCommand's generate action now reads ConstitutionStore, DomainStore, SpecificationRegistry, StrategyStore, TraceabilityStore, and ValidationEvidenceStore in parallel alongside the existing five reads, passing everything through to projectStateToTwin. No new CLI flags or commands were added.

decisions.statement: autoforge why now surfaces validation-gate evidence linked to a matched decision's related work
decisions.reasoning: autoforge gate check already recorded durable, structured evidence via ValidationEvidenceStore, but it was invisible to autoforge why -- closing the Validation to Observation to Evidence segment of the north-star's full loop required surfacing it in decision search, mirroring how learning-evidence is already surfaced.
consequences: formatDecisionMatches gains a Validation: <gateId> (<status>) line beneath a matched decision when validation evidence references any of that decision's related work items, derived by matching workId rather than a stored foreign key. No new CLI flags.

decisions.statement: gate check now stamps recorded evidence with the active work item's id
decisions.reasoning: Live end-to-end audit of the v0.24 continuous product evolution loop found gate check never attached workId, so why's validation surfacing (Task 6) was dead in practice despite passing all unit tests. Fixed by reading activeWork from WorkState and attaching its id when present.
consequences: Validation gate results now correctly flow through to autoforge why for any decision linked to the active work item; evidence recorded with no active work correctly omits workId.

decisions.statement: Documented AutoForge's full capability surface for agentic AI in the existing agentic AI guide
decisions.reasoning: Agents following AGENTS.md/README onboarding could see command syntax in AUTOFORGE_CLI_REFERENCE.md but had no map of which domain to reach for and when, especially post-v0.23/v0.24 (strategy, twin, validation evidence). Extended the existing guide rather than creating a second overlapping doc.
consequences: Agents onboarding to any AutoForge-managed project now have a single canonical doc covering both workflow etiquette and the full capability map, reducing the chance of missing a relevant domain (e.g. reaching for orchestrate prioritize instead of strategy assess, or never discovering learning/evidence or the digital twin).

decisions.statement: AutoForge v0.25 will establish separate Core, Agent, Web, and hosted Service boundaries in one compatibility-first monorepo migration
decisions.reasoning: AutoForge v0.24 already contains the project-intelligence engines; separating the deterministic model-independent Core from the first-party agentic interface prevents provider, credential, billing, and conversational concerns from coupling to the orchestration framework while preserving equal integration for third-party agents.
consequences: The existing @cojacklabs/autoforge package and autoforge executable remain compatible during v0.25.
The Core interactive TUI is deprecated and its useful interaction concepts move to AutoForge Agent.
Protocol, Core, and SDK boundaries are extracted before production Web, Service, payments, or cloud synchronization work begins.

decisions.statement: The canonical v0.25 north-star now defines a platform architecture migration rather than an interactive Core TUI
decisions.reasoning: The v0.24 project-intelligence lifecycle is complete, and embedding conversational interaction, model providers, credentials, tools, and hosted concerns in Core would violate model independence and create a competing project-truth boundary. The reconciled roadmap therefore makes protocol, Core, SDK, deterministic CLI, and structured handoffs authoritative, while preserving the prior TUI work as AutoForge Agent prototype material.
consequences: docs/planning/0.25/PLATFORM_MIGRATION_PLAN.md is the authoritative Core v0.25 implementation plan.
The prior v0.25 TUI design and implementation plan are historical and must not be executed against Core.
AutoForge Agent and future hosted products consume Core through supported interfaces and may not own parallel project state.

decisions.statement: AutoForge v0.25 will use a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo with independently versioned packages under the existing @cojacklabs scope; @cojacklabs/autoforge and the autoforge binary remain the deterministic Core CLI, while the interactive Agent ships separately as @cojacklabs/autoforge-agent and autoforge-agent.
decisions.reasoning: This preserves v0.24 installation and command compatibility while enforcing a model-independent Core, preventing hosted or provider dependencies from entering local project truth, and allowing Core, Agent, libraries, Web, and Service to mature on independent release cadences.
consequences: Source relocation must follow the documented acyclic dependency graph and publication gates; new public libraries begin at 0.1.0, Changesets records independent releases, and local Core operation cannot require an account or hosted service.

decisions.statement: The v0.25 package ownership and versioning policy is the source-relocation gate for task.define-package-ownership-and-versioning-policy.
decisions.reasoning: The policy resolves package identities, dependency directions, public and private distribution, release authority, independent semantic versions, command ownership, and compatibility promises before workspace restructuring begins.
consequences: The workspace foundation must implement the policy and pass its gates before any existing source is relocated.

decisions.statement: Bootstrap manifest reads are optional before scaffolding, and bootstrap status reports a successful not-scaffolded state with an explicit scaffold next action.
decisions.reasoning: A newly attached or long-lived project may validly lack the optional bootstrap manifest; surfacing raw ENOENT breaks the canonical agent onboarding sequence and obscures the safe initialization action.
consequences: Missing manifests resolve to null, status exits successfully with structured guidance, gates remain pending, approval returns a targeted invalid-state error, and malformed manifests continue to fail validation.

decisions.statement: AutoForge v0.25 adopts pnpm 11.22.0 and Turborepo 2.10.11 with temporary registered Core root tasks until source relocation creates real app and package workspaces.
decisions.reasoning: The existing @cojacklabs/autoforge package and autoforge binary must remain publishable and behavior-compatible during workspace foundation; Turborepo root tasks provide an incremental task graph without prematurely making the root private or creating empty placeholder packages.
consequences: pnpm-lock.yaml is the sole tracked dependency lockfile, package-lock.json is removed, apps/* and packages/* are workspace locations, workspace:* scripts exercise the current Core through Turbo, local caching is stored under ignored node_modules, remote caching is optional and disabled by default, and root-task aliases are removed when Core relocates to apps/core-cli.

decisions.statement: AutoForge enforces workspace boundaries with Turborepo import checks plus a repository-owned package policy, and CI separates affected-package validation from a mandatory full Core compatibility gate.
decisions.reasoning: Turbo boundaries catch undeclared imports and package breakout, while AutoForge's explicit manifest policy encodes the stricter Core, Agent, Web, and Service dependency graph; separate CI jobs keep incremental feedback fast without allowing affected filtering to skip the released Core baseline.
consequences: Every pull request runs built-in and AutoForge-specific boundary checks plus affected package tasks; every pull request and main push also runs full Core typechecking, foundation and legacy tests, formatting, planning synchronization, and package smoke validation without remote cache credentials.
